The user wants to arrange a flight on booking ID 1234 as soon as possible, and wants to check different options. They want to calculate the business class fare from the first airport in the available list to the last airport in the same list, on the last day of October 2024. Then provide estimated total payable amount.

We need to get the list of all airports. Then pick first and last. Then get flight cost for travel_date 2024-10-31, travel_from first airport, travel_to last airport, travel_class business. Then we need to compute total payable amount. But what does "total payable amount" refer to? Possibly the cost of the flight plus maybe insurance? The user didn't mention insurance. They just want estimated total payable amount. So likely just the flight cost. But maybe they want to include insurance? The user didn't mention insurance. So we can just provide the flight cost.

But we also need to arrange a flight on booking ID 1234. That means we need to book a flight. But we need an access token. We need to authenticate first. We need client_id, client_secret, refresh_token, grant_type, user_first_name, user_last_name. We don't have those. We might need to call travel_get_login_status to see if already logged in. But we don't have credentials. The user didn't provide them. We cannot proceed with booking. We can ask for credentials. But the user didn't provide them. We can respond asking for credentials. But the user didn't ask for that. They want us to do it. We can't. So we should ask for credentials or say we need them.

We can also get the nearest airport to a city. But we need a location. The user didn't specify a location. They want from the first to the last airport in the available list. So we need to get the list of all airports. Then get flight cost. Then we can provide the cost. But we also need to arrange a flight on booking ID 1234. That requires booking. We need an access token. We don't have one. We could call travel_get_login_status to see if there's an existing session. But we don't have credentials. We can call travel_get_login_status. Let's do that.
